messages.subject: temporal correlation within groups
parts:
I would like to confirm the proper way to specify INLA when modeling temporal correlation specific to different members of a group of interest. 

Here is sample code from a vignette of the glmmTMB package:

library(MASS)
library(glmmTMB)
library(INLA)

### generate data set ###

simid <- function(g, n=6, rho=0.7) {
  x <- mvrnorm(mu = rep(0,n),
               Sigma = rho ^ as.matrix(dist(1:n)) )   ## Simulate the process
  y <- x + rnorm(n)                               ## Add measurement noise
  times <- factor(1:n)
  id <- factor(rep(g,n)) ### create subjects in the group
  data.frame(y, times, id)
}
simid(1)
dat1 <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:1000, simid) )

### run glmmTMB and INLA AR1 models, with uniform hyperprior for the latter ###

tmb.1 <- glmmTMB(y ~ ar1(times + 0 | id), data=dat1)

UN.prior = "expression:
  log_dens = 0 - log(2) - theta / 2;
  return(log_dens);
"
inla.1 <- inla(y ~ f(times, replicate=id, model="ar1", hyper=UN.prior),
               data=dat1 %>% mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))))

The results appear to be very similar (INLA captures a similar intercept and a mean Rho estimate of .693, +/- .028).  

Is this INLA model correctly specified? I note, for example, that I used "replicate=" rather than "group=" within the AR1 function. The latter takes forever to run and perhaps is just wrong / unnecessary here. Are there any other flags or options that might be worth investigating when specifying temporal correlations relative to members of a single group in this manner?

Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] temporal correlation within groups
parts:
it seems correct to me (compared to how you generate them). yes, group
is the wrong thing, as you really replicate the data (independently),
they are not dependent over different 'id' (which 'group' can capture).

H
